1. (Currently amended) A method of using a finger palette to transfer cosmetics from a container to a destination, the method comprising:
a. providing a finger palette including: 
   i. a ring portion that is securable to a finger; and 
   ii. a surface portion secured to the ring portion, the surface portion being at least substantially smooth to allow a user to spread or blend cosmetic product on the surface portion, __wherein the surface portion is configured to receive cosmetic product from a source other than direct application from a cosmetics container__;
b. the method including the steps of:
   i. securing the finger palette to a finger;
   ii. depositing a cosmetic product onto the surface portion of the finger palette __using an applicator tool__; and
   iii. transferring the cosmetic product from the surface portion of the finger palette to a destination __using a transfer tool different from the applicator tool__.

2. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, further including the step of __first__ removing the cosmetic product from a container __using an extraction tool__ before depositing the cosmetic product onto the surface portion of the finger palette.

3. (Original) The method of claim 2 wherein:
a. the cosmetic product is removed from the container using a first instrument; and
b. the cosmetic product is transferred from the surface portion to the destination using a second instrument.

4. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1 wherein:
a. a first quantity of the cosmetic product is deposited onto the surface portion; and
b. a second quantity of the cosmetic product is transferred from the surface portion to the destination, the second quantity being smaller than the first quantity, __wherein the cosmetic product remaining on the surface portion after transfer is retained for blending with an additional cosmetic product__.

5. (Original) The method of claim 1 wherein:
a. the surface portion extends outwardly from a surface center to an outer perimeter; and
b. the surface portion is free, from any first point on the outer perimeter to any second point on the outer perimeter, of features that could trap cosmetics and complicate cleaning of the surface portion.

6. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1 wherein the surface portion is at least substantially without protrusions extending therefrom, __and wherein the surface portion is specifically designed to facilitate scraping of cosmetic product using an applicator tool in an uninterrupted motion__.

7. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1 wherein the surface portion is at least substantially planar, __and wherein the planar surface extends from a surface center to an outer perimeter without interruption__.

8. (Original) The method of claim 1 wherein the surface portion has a surface area between at least substantially 0.5 inches squared and at least substantially 6 inches squared.

9. (Original) The method of claim 8 wherein the surface portion has a surface area between 0.5 inches squared and 2 inches squared.

10. (Original) The method of claim 1 further including the step of spreading the cosmetic product on the surface portion before transferring the cosmetic product from the surface portion to the destination.

11. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1 wherein the finger palette is secured to the finger by passing the finger through the ring portion, __and wherein the ring portion is removably and replaceably securable to the finger__.

12. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1 wherein:
a. the cosmetic product is a first cosmetic product __removed from a first container using a first extraction tool__; and
b. the method further includes the step of depositing a second cosmetic product __removed from a second container using a second extraction tool__ onto the surface portion of the finger palette.

13. (Currently amended) The method of claim 12 wherein:
a. the first cosmetic product is deposited on a first segment of the surface portion; and
b. the second cosmetic product is deposited on a non-overlapping second segment of the surface portion, __such that the first and second cosmetic products remain separate on the surface portion prior to blending__.

14. (Original) The method of claim 12 further including the step of blending the first cosmetic product with the second cosmetic product on the surface portion to obtain a blended cosmetic product.

15. (Original) The method of claim 14 further including the step of transferring the blended cosmetic product from the surface portion of the finger palette to the destination.

16. (Original) The method of claim 12 wherein:
a. the first cosmetic product is removed from a first container and deposited on the surface portion using a first instrument;
b. the second cosmetic product is removed from a second container and deposited on the surface portion using a second instrument; and
c. the cosmetic product is transferred from the surface portion to the destination using a third instrument.

17. (Original) The method of claim 1 wherein:
a. the cosmetic product is nail makeup; and
b. the destination is a fingernail.

18. (Currently amended) A method of using a finger palette to transfer cosmetics from a container to a work surface, the method comprising:
a. providing a finger palette including:
   i. a ring portion configured to be removably and replaceably securable to a finger; and
   ii. a surface portion secured to the ring portion, the surface portion extending outwardly from a surface center to an outer perimeter, wherein the surface portion is at least substantially smooth so as to allow a user to scrape an applicator past the surface center in an uninterrupted motion while spreading or blending cosmetic product over the entirety of the surface portion, __and wherein the surface portion is specifically designed to facilitate controlled application and removal of cosmetic product__;
b. the method including the steps of:
   i. securing the finger palette to a finger by passing the finger through the ring portion;
   ii. __removing cosmetic product from a cosmetics container using a first extraction tool and__ placing a first quantity of the __extracted__ cosmetic product onto the surface portion of the finger palette;
   iii. removing cosmetic product from the surface portion of the finger palette __using a second application tool__; and
   iv. applying a second quantity of the removed cosmetic product to a destination, the second quantity being smaller than the first quantity.

19. (Currently amended) The method of claim 18 wherein:
a. the cosmetic product is __extracted from the cosmetics container using a first instrument__;
b. the cosmetic product is removed from the surface portion using a second instrument; and
c. the removed cosmetic product is applied to the destination using __the second instrument or a third instrument__.

20. (Currently amended) The method of claim 18 wherein:
a. the __extracted__ cosmetic product is a first cosmetic product __extracted from a first cosmetics container using a first extraction tool__; and
b. the method further includes the steps of:
   i. __extracting a second cosmetic product from a second cosmetics container using a second extraction tool and__ placing a third quantity of the __extracted second__ cosmetic product onto the surface portion of the finger palette; and
   ii. blending the first cosmetic product on the surface portion with the second cosmetic product on the surface portion to obtain a blended cosmetic product, wherein the cosmetic product applied to the destination is the blended cosmetic product.
